gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Techtest.org (Michael Barton, 10 March 2026) tested IKEA LADDA 2450 (article 50504692, the one IKEA US sells) and Eneloop Pro on the same bench: LADDA averaged 2,452 / 2,377 / 2,348 mAh at 0.2 / 0.5 / 1 A and Eneloop Pro averaged 2,563 / 2,441 / 2,419 mAh. That puts LADDA 3–4% behind Eneloop Pro, while standard Eneloop managed 1,940 / 1,862 / 1,879 mAh.
standout_why: Checked against the two pages ChatGPT cited. Digital Camera World (updated 2026-05-18) lists only spec-sheet figures for Eneloop Pro (2600 mAh, 85% after 1 year) and has no LADDA entry. The Which? sample shows LADDA reaching its rated 2,450 mAh, running 7:54 on one charge and losing 'about a third after 200 cycles', but it has no same-lab Eneloop or Eneloop Pro figure next to it. The Which? buying guide (2026-10-21) puts the Eneloop results and all retention scores behind sign-up. ChatGPT's own answer gives only rated mAh. No rival shows measured LADDA, Eneloop and Eneloop Pro capacity side by side at several discharge currents.
decides: Confirms LADDA 2450 as the value pick with a number behind it. The measured gap to Eneloop Pro is 2,377 vs 2,441 mAh at 0.5 A (−2.6%) and 2,348 vs 2,419 mAh at 1 A (−2.9%). In the same article IKEA was €7.99 per 4 and Eneloop Pro about €20 per 4. US prices from ChatGPT's cards: $11.99 vs $13.75. It also confirms that standard Eneloop holds about 500 mAh less (1,862 vs 2,377 mAh at 0.5 A), so for high-drain use the choice is LADDA or Pro, not standard Eneloop. Nothing found here changes the storage call: no named lab published a numeric retention figure for LADDA.
